about: Part of the reference catalogue: the case studies, designs and worked examples of chapters 1 to 4 of Goos and Jones,
Optimal Design of Experiments: A Case Study Approach (2011), for testing that software reproduces them. source: the
citation, with what was read and when. experiments: the extraction experiment of chapter 2, the same experiment
augmented with eight runs in chapter 3, and the peel strength experiment of chapter 4, each with its factors,
responses and runs as printed, where it is printed, and expected: every number the book prints for it, as printed
text, with where it is printed (a page and a quotation) and check: how to recompute it, or manual, the reason it is
not recomputed. A check with a disagreement records a number known not to reproduce and why. The book fits every
model in coded units, except chapter 4's prediction equations, and its VIF is n times a coefficient's variance in
units of sigma squared (Equation 2.13): the library's coefficient variance from evaluate_design's
information_matrix, times the run count. An alias matrix printed in thirds is compared entry by entry as arithmetic
(expression). Table 3.1's AICc is the model summary's aicc, and Table 3.2's recommended settings the corner of the
six factors where each model predicts the most yield (best_corner). designs: the splits of chapter 1's runs between
two machines or two treatments (allocate_runs: each split's variance, its root and its efficiency), Table 2.4's bias
calculation (product_column, the mean of a product column), the four-run design of Table 2.8, the D-optimal design
of Table 2.11, the designs of the coordinate-exchange example, each compared on |X'X| (information_matrix,
determinant), and chapter 4's D-optimal and I-optimal designs, compared on their relative variances, their average
prediction variance, their FDS plots and each other (relative_efficiency). not_captured: what in these pages is not
an experiment with data. Read with process_improve.experiments.reference_catalogue.reference_experiments;
tests/test_reference_catalogue.py recomputes every number that has a check.

experiments.notes: The book fits every model in coded units, x = (setting − centre)/(half the range), the factors x1 to x6 in the order of the columns. GeneBe's current process, methanol at neutral pH for 2 hours, yields about 25 mg; management wants more than 45 mg; at most 15 runs could be afforded, of which 12 are run and three kept for a confirmatory experiment. Dr. Zheng's model (Equation 2.1) keeps the main effects significant at the 5% level in the main-effects model, and the design being orthogonal, their coefficients are the same as in that model. The book's VIF is n times a coefficient's relative variance, its variance in units of σ² (Equation 2.13), checked as the library's coefficient variance times the run count.

runs.notes: Table 3.5 in its printed order: runs 1 to 12 are the original experiment (Table 2.3), and runs 13 to 20 the follow-up; Table 3.3 prints the same runs before the follow-up's yields were measured

experiments.notes: The book codes every factor -1 and +1, and the block +1 for the original runs and -1 for the follow-up (x7). Tables 3.1, 3.2 and 3.6 are fitted to the 12 original runs, the rest to all 20. Models 1, 7 and 8 of Table 3.1 hold the ethanol-by-propanol interaction without propanol's main effect: weak heredity. Table 3.6's caption names the interaction 'ethanol and butanol'; its row is ethanol by propanol, as Table 2.6's. Table 3.4's power is that of the t-test at the 5% level of a coefficient as large as the error's standard deviation, on the 6 degrees of freedom the 20 runs leave the 14-term model. The VIF is the book's, n times a relative variance.
